A.explanation: This is about $1/25$, the reciprocal of the correct frequency. It comes from dividing wavelength by speed instead of speed by wavelength.

B.explanation: About $13 \text{Hz}$ is the fundamental for $13.2 \text{ m}$ closed at both ends, where $L = \lambda/2$. That mode has an antinode in the middle, not the required node.

C.explanation: With nodes at both closed ends and at $6.6 \text{ m}$ in the middle, $L = \lambda = 13.2 \text{ m}$, so $f = 330/13.2 = 25 \text{Hz}$.

D.explanation: About $50 \text{Hz}$ gives $\lambda = 6.6 \text{ m}$ and also has a node halfway, but it is the next higher harmonic, not the lowest frequency.

hints: Notice the two closed doors must be displacement nodes, and the question also requires a displacement node $6.6 \text{ m}$ from each end.
Recall that the distance between two adjacent nodes in a stationary wave is $\lambda/2$, so use the $6.6 \text{ m}$ node spacing to find $\lambda$.
Connect wavelength to frequency with $v = f\lambda$ using $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and check why $L = \lambda/2$ cannot give a central node.
walkthrough: Identify the boundary conditions: both closed doors reflect sound with no air displacement, so there is a displacement node at $0$ and at $13.2 \text{ m}$.
The required pattern also has a node halfway, at $6.6 \text{ m}$. So nodes are at $0$, $6.6 \text{ m}$ and $13.2 \text{ m}$.
Use the stationary wave rule that adjacent nodes are $\lambda/2$ apart. Hence $\lambda/2 = 6.6 \text{ m}$, so $\lambda = 13.2 \text{ m}$.
This is the longest wavelength possible with that central node, so it gives the lowest frequency. A shorter wavelength such as $6.6 \text{ m}$ would also fit but gives a higher frequency.
Calculate frequency from $f = v/\lambda = 330/13.2$. This gives $f = 25 \text{Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$. This is option C.
